summary: Discovery call to understand Aurora AI's model selection needs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment options. Key concerns: long context window (20k+ tokens), multilingual (EN/ES/DE/JP) quality, tool-calling for structured orchestration, and enterprise security (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Redwood AE+SE outlined model families (Llama 3 variants, Mistral, RedPajama / Falcon alternatives), quantization/kv-cache tradeoffs, and suggested a benchmarking pilot with 10k-token prompts and multilingual test set.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE); Sofia Ramirez (Redwood SE); Liam Chen (CTO, Aurora AI); Priya Srinivasan (ML Engineer); Markus Vogel (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Sofia, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Liam: good, thanks. we've got about an hour, so want to dig into model selection and deployment options.
[00:11] Sofia: awesome. quick agenda, we want to understand your current stack, context length and multilingual needs, tool-calling/structured outputs, and security constraints - then we'll suggest candidate models and next steps. sound ok?
[00:22] Priya: yep sounds good.
[00:24] Markus: fine.
[00:26] Liam: quick context - Aurora's building a customer support + summarization product for enterprise clients in NA and EU. current infra is mostly in GCP, we use OpenAI for prototyping but seeing cost and latency at scale. key things: large context windows, multi-language (english, spanish, german, japanese), and the ability to call external tools to fetch user-specific data.
[00:47] Jordan: got it. and what context sizes are you seeing in production today?
[00:50] Priya: on average 4k tokens, but we have long threads and some legal docs that push to 15k-30k occasionally. for the new product we expect a lot more long context usage - ideally 20k+ native.
[01:06] Sofia: ok that helps. on the model side, do you have a preference for hosted vs dedicated vs private? any regulatory or data residency needs?
[01:14] Liam: we prefer host first for speed, but we need predictable cost and data isolation for some enterprise customers - likely dedicated or private for those. also security team will require SOC2 and KMS.
[01:26] Markus: yes, and SSO integration and audit logs. we may need on-prem for one large client.
[01:32] Jordan: makes sense - that aligns with what we do: hosted for quick time-to-value, dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and isolation, and private deployments for regulated on-prem scenarios.
[01:41] Sofia: on model capabilities - we usually look at open model families: Llama 3 (various sizes), Mistral-Instant/2, RedPajama, and then we compare against managed like OpenAI's longer-context variants. two big axes here: quality vs latency/cost, and native context support.
[01:58] Priya: are there Llama 3 variants that really do 20k+ comfortably? we've seen some vendors claim long context but it's actually chunking.
[02:06] Sofia: good question. some Llama 3 models have long-context variants or can be compiled with efficient attention kernels and kv cache optimizations; that plus compilation and kernel selection in the runtime gives better real-world performance than naive chunking. Quantization also affects memory footprint and speed - 4-bit can help but sometimes harms quality on multilingual tasks.
[02:30] Liam: multilingual - how do the open models compare for non-EN languages? japanese has been especially rough for us.
[02:37] Sofia: Mistral and some Llama 3 variants are decent in EU languages; for Japanese you might favor models with explicit Japanese pretraining or do instruction tuning on a Japanese dataset. we recommend evaluating per-language on your test prompts - which is why we'll ask for a representative prompt set.
[02:54] Priya: ok we'll pull that together.
[02:56] Jordan: tool calling - you mentioned needing to call external systems for per-user data; we support function/tool calling patterns and structured outputs. Sofia, maybe you can explain difference between simple webhook-style calls and richer tool oracles?
[03:06] Sofia: yeah - Redwood supports streaming responses + structured function-calling semantics. we can route to a microservice that returns structured JSON; the runtime preserves model state and kv cache so the latency for subsequent tokens is minimized. best practice is to keep tool outputs compact so they fit in the context; for very large external payloads you can store RAG vectors and fetch summaries.
[03:26] Liam: what's typical latency for a 70B model on dedicated capacity for a 2k token generation?
[03:31] Sofia: on dedicated GPU pools we've seen tail latencies around 300-450ms per request for generation at that size with optimized kernels and batching disabled for single user low-latency paths. depends on quantization and sequence length. hosted instances can be bursty but dedicated gives more predictable SLOs.
[03:48] Markus: from a security standpoint - how's data encrypted at rest? KMS integrations? audit logs?
[03:53] Jordan: we support customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private, and we have audit logs and RBAC in the console. we'll share the SOC2/ISO artifacts; private deployments can be air-gapped for that one on-prem client.
[04:04] Markus: good. can you send the SOC2 cert please?
[04:06] Jordan: absolutely, will include in the security pack.
[04:09] Sofia: for benchmarking, we suggest a small pilot: you provide a 10k-token-ish representative prompt set in English + translations for ES/DE/JP, we run a battery across 3-4 candidate models (Llama 3 70B quantized, Mistral-xx, RedPajama or Falcon alt) on hosted and dedicated to show latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.
[04:29] Priya: that would be ideal. what about function calling accuracy? can we instrument failure rates?
[04:34] Sofia: yes, we emit traces and per-route success metrics; you can map function call failures and hallucinations to a quality score. the console has tracing hooks and token-level cost breakdowns.
[04:45] Liam: curious about fallback behavior - if dedicated capacity is saturated, does traffic go to hosted?
[04:50] Jordan: yes, smart routing allows fallback to compatible model variants or regions by policy; you can configure automatic fallback or fail-open behavior.
[04:57] Priya: what's the uplift if we do 4-bit vs 8-bit quantization on those larger models?
[05:02] Sofia: 4-bit reduces memory substantially and can enable bigger context or larger batch sizes, lowering cost; but we've seen occasional quality regressions especially on multilingual or instruction-following tasks. we usually propose running both and comparing on your eval set.
[05:16] Liam: ok. on the cost side - what's a rough delta between hosted and dedicated per-token?
[05:21] Jordan: it varies by commit size. hosted is pay-as-you-go and slightly higher per-token; dedicated gives lower unit cost at the expense of committed monthly capacity. we'll include a sample TCO spreadsheet in the follow-up.
[05:33] Markus: for SSO we use SAML - supported?
[05:35] Jordan: yes, SAML/SSO supported, plus RBAC controls.
[05:38] Liam: can you talk a bit more about the runtime - caching and kv cache - we saw big wins with prefix caching in other vendors.
[05:45] Sofia: sure - Redwood's serving runtime does continuous batching and KV cache management; prefix caching can serve frequent prompts from cache and reduce per-token compute. also automatic batching for bursty workloads and policy-based routing lets you preserve latency SLOs.
[06:00] Priya: any gotchas on multilingual tokenization? we saw token inflation with Japanese.
[06:05] Sofia: tokenization can inflate in CJK languages; sometimes it's better to use models/tokenizers trained with explicit CJK or use subword vocab tuned for that language. we'll include tokenizer stats from our benchmarks.
[06:15] Jordan: let's walk through potential model shortlist - Sofia?
[06:18] Sofia: i'd propose 3 primary candidates for your pilot: Llama 3 70B variant (with long-context build), Mistral-instant family (strong for EU languages), and a RedPajama/Falcon alternative for cost-sensitive workloads. as a control we can run OpenAI's long-context endpoint to compare quality/loss for critical prompts.
[06:37] Liam: are there licensing or export complications with Llama 3 variants?
[06:40] Sofia: depends on the model license. we'll flag any T&Cs; Redwood's model catalog includes vetted performance and license notes.
[06:47] Priya: for tool calling pattern - do you support the function schema style (like openai function calling) or is it proprietary?
[06:53] Sofia: we support similar style function schemas and structured outputs. we can stream partial JSON with delta updates and perform a reconciliation step.
[07:02] Liam: deployment plan - we want a pilot on hosted, then move to dedicated for customers that require isolation, and on-prem for that single regulated client. timeline target: pilot in august, production by october.
[07:14] Jordan: sounds reasonable. we'll aim to have pricing and pilot plan by Friday (2025-07-24).
[07:18] Priya: for the pilot, what do you need from us?
[07:20] Sofia: 1) representative prompt set (with language breakdown), 2) a few production-like queries that exercise tool-calling, 3) expected success criteria (latency, accuracy, hallucination thresholds).
[07:30] Priya: we'll prepare that.
[07:32] Markus: one more security question: do you support customer-managed keys for hosted or only for dedicated/private?
[07:37] Jordan: customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we provide encryption at rest with our keys but can discuss custom arrangements for enterprise customers.
[07:48] Liam: ok. anything else on cost controls?
[07:51] Sofia: Redwood Optimize provides batching/caching suggestions and model recommendations by workload; that often yields 20-40% unit cost reduction.
[08:01] Jordan: quick recap - we'll send: pricing + Dedicated options, security pack (SOC2/ISO/KMS docs), model comparison spreadsheet, and propose dates for a pilot. next steps capture.
[08:13] Liam: good.
[08:15] Priya: couple micro questions - for telemetry, retention policy, and PII handling?
[08:19] Jordan: telemetry retention configurable on Dedicated/Private; hosted has default retention but can be extended. PII redaction and opt-out can be configured; we'll send the policy doc.
[08:30] Sofia: also note, when evaluating quality, include post-edit cost for non-english languages in the TCO.
[08:36] Priya: noted.
[08:38] Jordan: any blockers to getting the pilot running in August?
[08:41] Liam: need to align internal stakeholders but should be ok. security will want the docs before sign-off.
[08:46] Jordan: understood. we'll aim to get that to Markus.
[08:49] Markus: thanks.
[08:51] Jordan: great - we'll follow up with the artifacts. thanks everyone.
[08:55] Liam: thanks.

[End of call]

Notes: transcript has occasional minor transcription artifacts (names sometimes garbled), some speaker overlaps. The call covered qualification, model family tradeoffs, context length requirements (~20k+), multilingual concerns (esp Japanese), function-calling/structured output, security/compliance, and a pilot plan.
